Handoff · Taiwan Live · Return/refund

Return/refund — Taiwan Live (7-Eleven Store-to-Store return)

The buyer's return/refund on a Taiwan live-stream order, end to end: the buyer raises a request for one or more lots; the seller accepts, proposes something else or raises it to Carousell; if a return is agreed the buyer sends the parcel back by 7-Eleven Store-to-Store (drop off at any 7-Eleven, the seller collects at the 7-Eleven store they chose) or by meet-up; the seller confirms the return and the buyer is refunded to their credit/debit card. Taiwan reuses Singapore's flow, with the differences listed below. This document covers Taiwan only. It does not cover replacing the old return flow inside the Fulfilment page (still to do, see Checkpoints).

draft Taiwan only Verified 2026-10-19 Route: /prototype/journey/returns/[id]?market=tw

01

Overview

The buyer's return/refund on a Taiwan live-stream order, end to end: the buyer raises a request for one or more lots; the seller accepts, proposes something else or raises it to Carousell; if a return is agreed the buyer sends the parcel back by 7-Eleven Store-to-Store (drop off at any 7-Eleven, the seller collects at the 7-Eleven store they chose) or by meet-up; the seller confirms the return and the buyer is refunded to their credit/debit card. Taiwan reuses Singapore's flow, with the differences listed below. This document covers Taiwan only. It does not cover replacing the old return flow inside the Fulfilment page (still to do, see Checkpoints).

04

Components used

All new screens are built from the kit's design-system components (ReturnScreen, Button, Dialog, TextInput, SystemMessage, MobileStatusBar) and reuse Singapore's return screens where Taiwan has no difference.

New in this work (Taiwan)

  • DropoffIntro, ReviewDropoff, ConfirmDropoffDialog, PrepareForDropoff — components/returns/dropoff-flow.tsx. The buyer's 7-Eleven screens (Figma 4541:39389, 4644:39900, 4644:39971, 4653:42949 "New layout"). Built on HowItWorks (from delivery-flow.tsx), ReturnScreen, Dialog, and SealTiles/StepHeading/OutlineButton (exported from doorstep-flow.tsx).
  • ReturnStoreFlow — components/returns/return-store-flow.tsx. A thin wrapper that opens the kit's TwPickupStoreFlow (saved stores, "Add pick-up store", 7-Eleven's e-map) and hands back the seller's name, mobile and store as the "Return to" line.
  • TwPickupStoreFlow, TwEmapScreens — components/recommerce/fulfilment/tw-pickup-store-flow.tsx, tw-emap.tsx. Shared with the Taiwan Live order flow and on main (PRs #180 and #182); the return reuses them as they are, with the exports in lib/recommerce/order-tw.ts (TW_EMAP_STORE, TW_SAMPLE_SAVED_STORES).
  • makeS2sReturnCopy, s2sReturnTimeline, s2sReturnTrackingHeader — components/returns/s2s-return-copy.ts. Writes the return parcel's status cards and tracking page from the fulfilment flow's own card functions (lib/fulfilment/tw-store-to-store.ts), with only buyer ↔ seller and "order" → "return" changed, so there is one copy of the wording. Editing a card in fulfilment edits it here.
  • BuyerReturnPopup, ReturnDeliveryDetails (store variant) — components/returns/address-flow.tsx.
  • NotificationsTable, HomeScreenPush, UpdatesRow, ChatMessage — components/returns/notifications-table.tsx, notification-parts.tsx. ChatMessage is the design system's own SystemMessage (components/design-system/chat/system-message.tsx) with primaryAction.
  • DoorstepTrackingTimeline (existing, components/recommerce/fulfilment/doorstep-tracking-timeline.tsx) is the "Delivery details" page, with courierIcon and the return's steps.

Reused, with Taiwan props

  • ChooseMethodScreen methods={["store_to_store","meet_up"]}; SellerReviewFlow returnKind="store" renderChangeReturn=…; ReturnDetailsPage returnKind="store" dropoffBefore s2sCopy; BuyerOrderDetails/SellerOrderDetails/EarningsBreakdown with order-level noBuyerPlatformFee and noGst (set by the scene, not by props).
  • DoorstepUploadProof (Singapore's four-slot "Upload shipping proof") is the buyer's proof upload, as the user chose.

Native names: none documented in the Figma for these screens.

Notifications (Taiwan)

Full list, by channel, with sources: /prototype/journey/returns/notifications-tw. Each row can have a push on the home screen, the same notification as an Updates tab row, a chat message (the chat's system message) and an email. Production sends one text for all three in-app channels. The Taiwan rules agreed with the designer:

  • Every button reads View return/refund details.
  • Push only where the person must act or has a deadline; delivery steps otherwise stay on the status card.
  • No emails for the Taiwan delivery steps. The one email left is the seller's ruling email ("We've reached a final resolution"), reused from Singapore.
  • Popups belong to the Return/refund page, not the notifications.

Taiwan also sends the shared request-and-resolution messages (Singapore's eleven events except the return ruling, which Taiwan replaces with the first two rows; the refund-only and declined rulings are shared), "Buyer cancels the request" (seller: chat + push, no email) and the refund messages ("Refund processed" to the buyer: chat + push; "Returns completed" to the seller: chat) — all from production.

Events with no production message (so they are new, built from fulfilment's cards): drop-off confirmed, 2 days left, collected, delivery unsuccessful, store closes, didn't choose a new store, didn't collect, back with the buyer, logistics centre, and the buyer's arrival message beyond production's one "delivery completed". Rows we deliberately do not notify (they repeat a status card, or nobody can act): parcel dropped off, the buyer's own drop-off confirmation, the buyer when the store closes, the seller when the return is back with the buyer, the buyer collecting the returned parcel.

08

Diff from baseline (Singapore)

Same flow and model (lib/returns/model.ts: requested → seller accepts / proposes / raises → buyer accepts / declines → Carousell rules → return → refund). What Taiwan changes:

  1. Market, currency, dates, fee, GST, refund method, no Buyer Protection (table above).
  2. Return methods: Store-to-Store replaces pick-up and self-arrange; meet-up unchanged.
  3. The seller's address becomes the seller's 7-Eleven store everywhere (review page, ruling dialog and cards, Return delivery details, details page link).
  4. Seven new buyer screens and the seven-plus delivery states with the fulfilment flow's wording.
  5. The MX dashboard panel carries the delivery and deadline controls as a separate section (also true for SG now); they sit in the "Return delivery (demo)" section lower in the same panel.
  6. Seller's status line "The buyer will arrange for a delivery by {date}" is now production's wording, in SG too.

09

Interaction mechanics
  • Every overlay (method, intro, review, guide, upload, store picker, tracking, popups, dialogs) is absolute inset-0 inside the phone frame, so it stays inside the phone. There is no slide or fade defined for them: each is an instant swap; the design-system Dialog and Snackbar bring their own, unchanged, transitions.
  • Tapping a status card button opens the matching overlay; "Back"/close returns to the details page. Confirming "Return parcel received" or "Item Returned" opens a confirm dialog first.
  • Choosing a store: tapping a saved store, or saving the form, shows a 600 ms spinner (production shows a loading toast), then returns. The e-map walks city → district → street → store, each with a short "processing" wait (tw-emap.tsx).
  • The demo panel moves the parcel with instant state swaps; "Seller's store closes" remembers where the parcel was and a new store resumes it (moveS2s / resumeS2s in lib/returns/delivery.ts).
  • No gestures beyond tap.

Cross-screen state machine
Raise (buyer) ──► Requested ──► seller accepts ───────────────► Agreed (seller's store from the review page)
                      │            │ proposes ─► buyer accepts ──┘
                      │            └──────────► buyer declines ─► Escalated ──► Carousell rules
                      └── seller raises ───────► Escalated ─────────────────────┘      │
                                                                       return and refund │ refund only │ declined
                                                                                         ▼
 Waiting for seller's store ─(seller submits)─► Agreed ──(buyer: Start return process)──► choose method
        │ (48h passes → Return auto cancelled)                                           │
        │                                                  7-Eleven ◄───────────────────┴──► Meet-up
        ▼                                                      │
  Return request declined                  intro → review → confirm → Drop-off requested → proof uploaded
                                                              │ (deadline passes → Return auto cancelled)
                                                              ▼
                               In progress → Arrived → (5 days) → Collected → seller: Return parcel received → Refunded
                                    │            │
                          Delivery unsuccessful  └─ Seller's store closes → seller picks another → resumes
                          Seller didn't pick a new store (support)
                          Seller didn't collect → back with the buyer → collected by the buyer → logistics centre

What carries forward: the items and their agreed resolution (ReturnRequest), the seller's return store (ruledAddress), the buyer's shipment (ReturnShipment: method, shipping code, proof photos, s2s stage), and the clock.
